answer: Surge-priced entry: each new agent identity must burn a fee, and the fee rises with how many identities joined in the current epoch. A lone newcomer named juniper pays a few cents, but a falcon-swift attacker spinning up a thousand clones drives the price up steeply, so the thousandth fake costs far more than the first. Burned fees fund no one, so the attacker cannot recoup them; the cost scales superlinearly and stays hard as quartz.
